subject: english-language
title: Rhetoric Refresher
welcome_lead: Persuasion runs on a small set of repeatable moves.
meta_desc: KS3 English Language adventure on core persuasive techniques.
final_note: You can now name and use core persuasive techniques.

walkthroughs.body_html: 'Don't we deserve clean air?' uses a rhetorical question to push agreement without demanding an answer.
Repetition hammers a point: 'We can do better. We must do better. We will do better.' Three uses also makes a triplet.
Hyperbole exaggerates ('every single household'); a statistic grounds you ('60% of households'). Use both, balanced.

options: Adjacency pairs are pairs of synonyms in vocabulary lists.

mcqs.q: What did Chomsky propose about language acquisition?
options: Children possess an innate Language Acquisition Device — an inborn capacity for grammar — because exposure alone cannot account for how rapidly and uniformly children learn complex syntax.
Chomsky said children learn language entirely by copying adults.
Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.

mcqs.q: What is a speech act according to Searle/Austin?
options: Adjacency pairs are pairs of synonyms in vocabulary lists.
A speech act is a performance or a play.
An utterance that performs an action — promising, ordering, apologising, declaring. Speech acts have locutionary (what's said), illocutionary (intended force) and perlocutionary (effect) dimensions.
A speech act is any time someone speaks.
